hypotheses.paper: conclusion « conjugués relativement à W ∩ D »
hypotheses.note: (a) SontConjugues (W ∩ D) (L ⊓ D) (L' ⊓ D) and L ⊓ D ⊔ L' ⊓ D = D; (b) additionally Disjoint (L ⊓ D) (L' ⊓ D), span (W ∩ D) = D; (c) IsSommeConvexes (W ∩ D) ![…]

findings: Theorem 1 (l.452–456) is true under all three readings of Déf. 4 (OQ-163 (a), (b), (c)), so its mark does not depend on the ruling. Under (a) the printed proof (l.460–501) does not apply: it uses P_L « parallèlement à L′ », which exists only when L ⊕ L′ = E. Under (a) a different proof works: write a = x + y with x ∈ L ∩ W, y ∈ L′ ∩ W, and project along the supplementary conjugate N of D. P_D maps L into L and L′ into L′ (this is the (b) step applied to (D, N) and the supplementary conjugates of L, L′), so a = P_D x + P_D y with both terms in D. This proof uses neither D′ nor the pair (D, D′) (theoreme1_distingues).

Under (b) the printed proof (l.480–501) formalizes as written. The step « P_L(a) ∈ D » for a ∈ W ∩ D (l.481) extends to every a ∈ D only because D ∩ W spans D, which uses « W engendrant E ». The theorem's conclusion that L ⊓ D and L′ ⊓ D are supplementary in D also uses it; that conclusion is not printed, but Theorem 2's inf needs it.
questions: OQ-163: Theorem 1 is stated and proved under (a), (b) and (c). The decl of record is Benzecri.theoreme1, reading (a). If the ruling is (b), the anchor should be theoreme1_supplementaires, whose conclusion includes supplementarity in D; if (c), theoreme1_sommeConvexes. No Lean changes either way.

questions: The Lemma is stated with IsCompl L L′ because « la projection sur L parallèlement à L′ » is defined only for a supplementary pair. Under OQ-163 (a), with L, L′ not supplementary, the Lemma has no meaning. Reading taken: (b). Left unmarked until the ruling. If the author agrees that the notation P_L already presupposes L ⊕ L′ = E, then IsCompl is not an added hypothesis and the row can be marked as it stands.

kb_proposals: Chapter3/Conjugues: for a supplementary conjugate pair (L, L′), L.projection L′ h maps W into L ∩ W (projection_mem_inter), and it maps every distinguished D into D (projection_mem_of_mem). Theorem 2's inf/sup and the Boolean-algebra work should start from these lemmas.
Reading (a) of Déf. 4 reduces to (b) by projecting along the chosen conjugate (conjugue W D or EstDistingue's witness): P_D preserves every distinguished subspace. See theoreme1_distingues.
